questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride is added to phenol in cold aqueous NaOH (273–278 K). The product is:
questions.explain: The diazonium ion attacks the para carbon of the phenoxide ion and both nitrogens are kept, giving the orange azo dye p-HO–C₆H₄–N=N–C₆H₅. Loss of N₂ belongs to replacement reactions, not coupling.

questions.q: For coupling a diazonium salt with aniline, the reaction medium should be:
questions.explain: In mild acid the NH₂ group is the stronger activator and the diazonium salt stays intact. Strong acid would protonate the amine and deactivate the ring, while strong base destroys the diazonium ion; mild base suits phenols.

questions.q: Methyl orange is prepared by coupling:
questions.explain: Diazotised 4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid couples at the para position of N,N-dimethylaniline. Anthranilic acid gives methyl red, and benzidine with naphthionic acid gives Congo red.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with β-naphthol (2-naphthol) in NaOH. The position of attack on the naphthol is:
questions.explain: In naphthalenes coupling goes ortho to the OH at the α-carbon, so β-naphthol is attacked at C-1, giving the orange-red 1-phenylazo-2-naphthol. The para-rule for benzene rings does not carry over directly.
